Lists, indices and traversal

Unit 1 · Week 6 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Python editor, paper index/value grids and the arrays chapter. Use suitable integer input.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Lists, indices and traversal

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Success means load a list, identify a value by index and display each index/value pair. Explain that Python lists implement these array-style tasks. Lists can change size and hold mixed types, while some arrays have a fixed size/type. Use consistent integer values in this week’s exercises.

2. Retrieval: repeated input

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and pair explanation

Allow a minute without notes, then compare. range(3) gives 0,1,2 and three passes. A running total combines inputs but does not retain each original value. Ask why storing all readings might help later. This leads to a list without suggesting lists and fixed-size arrays are identical.

3. A position differs from its value

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example and guided prediction

Model scores=[12,7,19]. The first non-negative index is 0, scores[1] is 7 and len(scores) is 3. Ask for index of value 19:2. The last valid non-negative index is len(scores)-1. Python also supports negative indexing, which is outside this introductory convention. One-dimensional access uses one index.

4. Loading values with append

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher think-aloud and code annotation

Trace suitable integer inputs 12,7,19. The empty list grows to [12], then [12,7], then [12,7,19]. append adds at the end. Initialising scores=[] happens once before repetition. int converts input text. Ask learners to mark repeated instructions and predict len(scores) after each pass:1,2,3.

5. Traversal with each index

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example and faded support

Expected output pairs 0 12,1 7,2 19. range(len(scores)) produces 0,1,2, so every stored element is visited once. Learners identify which expression is an index and which accesses a value. Support: provide a three-column trace. Stretch: explain why range(len(scores)+1) would attempt an invalid final index.

6. Your loading and display program

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired programming with role changes

Pairs load four integers then print each index/value pair. Use 8,3,6,10: indices 0..3 and matching values. Driver types loading, navigator checks a trace, then swap for display. Every learner records predictions. Support: supply an empty list and loop headers. Stretch: replace a source value and explain why its index stays the same. Keep suitable input assumption explicit.

7. Where is the last valid index?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: All-student hinge question

For [12,7,19], correct B is 2. A is last value 19, C is length 3. scores[3] raises IndexError. Collect simultaneous choices before discussion. If several choose C, label positions on paper and recheck a two-element list. Do not imply all out-of-range Python indices are positive.

8. Exit ticket: access and explain

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit ticket

For values=[8,3,6], values[1]=3, length 3 and last valid non-negative index 2. Access uses square brackets; append adds one value. Collect individual answers to identify indexing or length support for accumulator traversal next lesson.
